feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: NPR's expanded coverage of U.S. and world politics, the latest news from Congress and the White House and elections.

entry.title: Trump says developing AI is a critical race, downplaying fears
entry.summary: President Trump continues to support frontier artificial intelligence development, despite industry fears such technology could destroy humanity, casting AI as a critical race against China.

entry.title: Sen. Bernie Sanders says Congress has gotten a 'wake-up call' on AI risks
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with U.S. Sen. Bernie Sanders,I-Vermont, about his concerns over the risks of artificial intelligence.

entry.title: This bill could reshape crypto in America -- and it's sparking a major battle
entry.summary: The legislation would establish rules of the road for the crypto sector for the first time — but opponents are up in arms, and the bill faces an uncertain prospect in the Senate.

entry.title: Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon to share a stage to promote curbs on AI
entry.summary: The poles of U.S. politics are coming together over AI. Sanders and Bannon will appear at the "Pro-Human Assembly" in Washington, D.C., to convince Congress to work faster to curb the impact of AI.

entry.title: The Supreme Court rejects Trump's mail voting restrictions for this year's midterms
entry.summary: The Supreme Court has rejected the Trump administration's request to allow mail-in voting restrictions under a U.S. Postal Service plan for the midterm general election.

entry.title: Mitch McConnell returns to Senate after fall that led to an extended medical absence
entry.summary: McConnell spent weeks in recovery before explaining he was "briefly unconscious" following the fall that sent him to the hospital and a weeks-long recovery process.

entry.title: Federal agents may have broken state laws in voter fraud hunt, whistleblower claims
entry.summary: Federal agents may have broken state laws after the Department of Homeland Security began surging personnel for what it called the Unlawful Voter Initiative, a federal whistleblower alleges.

entry.title: What's next for Senator John Fetterman?
entry.summary: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Adam Jentleson, former chief of staff for Pennsylvania Democratic Senator John Fetterman, about recent revelations about Sen. Fetterman's work performance.

entry.title: Kennedy Center says it's on the brink of bankruptcy, might close as early as Tuesday
entry.summary: In two board resolutions made public Monday, the arts institution says it is in a dire financial and physical state — and that only President Trump can "rescue" it.

entry.title: Texas Rep. Greg Casar discusses bill to temporarily pause advanced AI development
entry.summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with U.S. Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, about his efforts to regulate artificial intelligence.
